title: Open direct image Tor bound over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small étale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $a\le b$ be integers and $e\ge0$ an integer. Let $L\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Suppose $R^qj_*F=0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] for every $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every $q>e$. Suppose also that, for every finite $A$-module $M$, the natural projection map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] for the derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]
$$ (Rj_*L)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_T\longrightarrow Rj_*(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_V) $$
is an isomorphism, where $M_S$ denotes the constant module sheaf on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Then $Rj_*L$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+e]$, tested against every $A_T$-module sheaf.

source.place: Step 3, passage from finite constant-module Tor tests for Rj_* L to all module sheaves by stalks and filtered unions.

proof.text: Apply the finite constant-module test theorem to the data in the statement. Its hypotheses are precisely the given Tor amplitude, uniform direct-image vanishing and finite projection isomorphisms, so all finite constant tensor tests of Rj_*L vanish outside [a,b+e].
Apply the stalk and filtered-colimit extension theorem with Q=Rj_*L and interval [a,b+e] to those finite tests. It gives the required Tor amplitude against every module sheaf.

proof_origin.place: Composition of the proved finite-test bound (original steps 1--3) with the stalk and filtered-union extension (original steps 4--6), T3.

The delivery has no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. Its hypotheses (Tor amplitude [a,b], uniform R^q j_* vanishing for q>e, projection isomorphism for finite constant M) are exactly what the citer supplies from its own steps 1–2 and from lem-sf-projection-finite-constant, and it keeps the arbitrary field. The coefficients are ordinary constant-A étale module sheaves throughout. Duplicate search over the DAG found no node stating the item: det-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-open-tor needs k separably closed, and thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude needs k algebraically closed and constructible K. Checks by step: step 1 tests the hypothesis with M_V. Step 2 gets the lower bound from an injective representative that is zero below a (dplus-injective-representative (1), right-derived-plus-injective (2)). Step 3 applies lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound; all its hypotheses hold. Steps 4 and 6 use the stalk, monoidal-pullback, stalk-cohomology, constant-stalk and conservativity lemmas, at the same level of detail as the accepted det-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-open-tor step 9. Step 5 applies lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor with R=A to the finitely generated submodules; this diagram is small and filtered, its colimit is N, and each submodule is finite. Edge cases checked: A=0, V or T empty, e=0, a=b, and Z/ell^2 coefficients, where finite modules can have infinite projective dimension. One repaired fault (C1/E5): step 3 silently identified three versions of the derived direct image — the upper-bound lemma's unbounded total RF, the bounded-below Rj_* of step 2 and the K-injective Rj_* in the projection morphism. The fixed step 3 shows all three equal Q(j_* I_M), citing prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist and lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived.
